<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CATALYST SEMICONDUCTOR, INC.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During fiscal 2007, the Company granted approximately
1,542,000 stock options with an estimated total grant date fair value of $1.9
million and a weighted average grant date fair value of $1.25 per option. During
fiscal 2007, the Company recorded stock-based compensation expense related to
stock options of $2,096,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During fiscal 2007, the Company granted 225,000 shares
of restricted stock with a total grant date fair value of $732,000 and a
weighted average grant date fair value of $3.25 per share. The restricted stock
vests over a period of three years with 1/3 of the grant vesting at the end of
each year. There were no shares of restricted stock outstanding at the
beginning of the year. During fiscal 2007, the Company recorded stock-based
compensation expense related to restricted stock of $98,000. Through fiscal
2007, no shares vested or forfeited. As of April&nbsp;29, 2007, there were
225,000 unvested shares of restricted stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of April&nbsp;29, 2007, the aggregate amount of
unearned stock-based compensation expense, net of estimated forfeitures,
related to stock options was $3.2 million, which the Company will recognize
over an estimated weighted average amortization period of 2.6&nbsp;years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of April&nbsp;29, 2007, the aggregate amount of
unearned stock-based compensation expense, net of estimated forfeitures,
related to restricted stock was $587,000, which the Company will recognize over
an estimated weighted average amortization period of 2.6&nbsp;years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stock-based compensation
expense capitalized in inventory at April&nbsp;29, 2007 was not material.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Valuation Assumptions</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During
fiscal 2007, fiscal 2006 and fiscal 2005, the Company continued to utilize the
Black-Scholes model for calculating the estimated fair value of stock-based
compensation awards granted under the Company&#146;s stock option plans. The
expected term and volatility estimates are based on the Company&#146;s historical
experience. The fair value of stock options granted under the Company&#146;s stock
option plans were estimated at the date of grant using a straight-line attribution
method with the following weighted average assumptions:</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CATALYST SEMICONDUCTOR, INC.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Equity Incentive Programs:</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Overview</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company considers equity compensation to be long
term compensation and an integral component of efforts to attract and retain
exceptional executives, senior management and world-class employees. The
Company believes that properly structured equity compensation aligns the
long-term interests of stockholders and employees by creating a strong, direct
link between employee compensation and stock appreciation, as stock options are
only valuable to the Company&#146;s employees if the value of the Company&#146;s common
stock increases after the date of grant.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s board of
directors has approved a common stock repurchase program that is described
below.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2003 Stock Incentive Plan</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In October&nbsp;1989, the Company adopted a founder stock
plan for incentive stock options and non-statutory stock options. The founder
stock plan was amended and restated in March&nbsp;1993 as the Stock Option
Plan, which had the effect of extending its expiration date to March&nbsp;2003.
In January&nbsp;1999 and September&nbsp;2000, the stockholders authorized an
additional 1.8&nbsp;million shares and 2.5&nbsp;million shares, respectively,
to be reserved under the 1993 Stock Option Plan (the &#147;1993 Plan&#148;). In December&nbsp;2002,
the stockholders approved an amendment and restatement of the 1993 Plan,
renaming it the 2003 Stock Incentive Plan (&#147;SIP&#148;), extending its expiration
date to November&nbsp;2012, authorized an additional 1.0 million shares and a
provision to automatically authorize annual additions to the plan on the first
day of each fiscal year of 1.0&nbsp;million shares or 5% of the then
outstanding shares, whichever is less. A total of 7.4 million shares of common
stock have been reserved for issuance under the SIP. The SIP allows for the
issuance of incentive and non-statutory stock options, restricted stock,
restricted stock units and stock appreciation rights. Options granted under the
SIP are for periods not to exceed 10 years. Incentive stock option and
non-statutory stock option grants under the SIP generally must be at prices
equal to 100% of the fair market value of the stock at the date of grant. Options
generally vest over four years. Restricted stock units represent the right to
receive shares of common stock in the future, with the right to future delivery
of the shares subject to a risk of forfeiture or other restrictions that will
lapse upon satisfaction of specified conditions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;28, 2006,
the compensation committee of the board of directors approved the grant of
restricted stock to certain executive officers of the Company pursuant to the
Company&#146;s SIP. The grant of the restricted stock to each of the executive
officers vest over a period of three years with 1/3 of the grant vesting at the
end of each year.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2003 Director Stock Option Plan</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 1993, the Company
adopted the 1993 Director Stock Option Plan (the &#147;1993 Director SOP&#148;), which
provides for the grant of non-statutory stock options to non-employee directors.
In November&nbsp;1999 and September&nbsp;2000, the stockholders authorized an
additional 100,000 and 450,000 shares, respectively, to be reserved under the
1993 Director SOP. In December&nbsp;2002, the stockholders approved an
amendment and restatement of the 1993 Director SOP, renaming it the 2003
Director Stock Option Plan (the &#147;2003 Director SOP&#148;) and extending its expiration
date to November&nbsp;2012. A total of 770,000 shares of common stock have been
reserved for issuance under the 2003 Director SOP. Options granted under the
2003 Director SOP prior to May&nbsp;1, 2000 were for periods not to exceed five
years and not to exceed a period of </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">16</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-16',FILE='C:\Fc\1941532541_P66529CHE_2250547\18586-1-fo.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Jul 13 15:04 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CATALYST SEMICONDUCTOR, INC.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">10 years
for grants made thereafter. Option grants under the 2003 Director SOP must be
at prices equal to 100% of the fair market value of the stock at the date of
grant. Options granted prior to December&nbsp;2002 vested over a period of
three years. Options granted beginning in December&nbsp;2002 vest immediately
as of the date of the grant.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">1998 Special Equity Incentive Plan</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;1998, the Company adopted an
additional stock option plan entitled the 1998 Special Equity Incentive Plan (&#147;SEIP&#148;)
for incentive stock options and non-statutory stock options for certain
directors, officers and consultants of the Company. A total of 3.5&nbsp;million
shares of common stock have been reserved for issuance under the SEIP. Options
granted under the SEIP are for periods not to exceed 10 years. Options
generally vest over four years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A
summary of stock option and restricted stock activity under the SIP, the 2003
Director SOP and the SEIP is as follows (in thousands, except per share
amounts):</font></p>

2007, based on the $3.77 closing stock price of our common stock on the NASDAQ
Global Market, which would have been received by the option holders had all
option holders exercised their options as of that date. The total number of
in-the-money options outstanding and exercisable as of April&nbsp;29, 2007 and April&nbsp;30,
2006 was 3,513,000 and 2,078,000, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company settles
employee stock option exercises with newly issued shares of common stock. The
Company does not have any equity instruments outstanding other than the options
and restricted stock described above as of April&nbsp;29, 2007.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2001 Common Stock Repurchase Program</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September&nbsp;2001 and
subsequent periods, the Company&#146;s board of directors authorized a program for
the open market repurchase of up to an aggregate of 3.5&nbsp;million shares of
its common stock. Upon reaching the maximum number of shares authorized under
this program, the board of directors authorized a new stock repurchase program
in September&nbsp;2005 to repurchase up to 1.0 million shares of its common
stock. In subsequent periods, the board of directors amended the program and
authorized the purchase of up to an aggregate of 2.0 million shares. The
purpose of these share repurchase programs are to reduce the long-term
potential dilution in earnings per share that might result from issuances under
the Company&#146;s stock option plans and to take advantage of the relatively low
price of the Company&#146;s common stock. During fiscal 2007, fiscal 2006 and fiscal
2005, the Company repurchased 355,795, 912,943 and 1,901,176 shares,
respectively, for an approximate cost of $1.3 million, $4.5 million and $9.6
million, respectively<b>. </b>The Company
accounts for treasury stock using the cost method. Of the 2.0 million shares
currently authorized by the Company&#146;s board of directors for repurchase, the
Company has repurchased a total of 1,214,014 shares and, as of April&nbsp;29,
2007, can repurchase a total of 785,986 additional shares.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CATALYST SEMICONDUCTOR, INC.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 4&#151;Net Income
Per Share<a name="Note4netIncomePerShare_123705"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Basic
net income per share is computed by dividing net income available to common
stockholders (numerator) by the weighted average number of common shares
outstanding (denominator) during the period. Diluted net income per share is
computed using the weighted number of common shares and potentially dilutive
common shares outstanding during the period under the treasury stock method. Under
the treasury stock method, the effect of stock options outstanding is not
included in the computation of diluted net income per share for periods when
their effect is anti-dilutive, which in the current period includes
consideration of unearned stock-based compensation as required by SFAS No.&nbsp;123(R).
In computing diluted net income per share, the average stock price for the
period is used in determining the number of shares assumed to be purchased from
the exercise of stock options. A reconciliation of the basic and diluted per
share computations is as follows (in thousands, except per share data):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Options to purchase 5,385,000 shares of common stock
with an exercise price in excess of $3.77 per share outstanding during
fiscal&nbsp;2007, as well as unvested restricted stock were not included in the
computation of diluted income per share because they were anti-dilutive.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Options to purchase 2,278,000 shares of common stock
with an exercise price in excess of $4.80 per share outstanding during
fiscal&nbsp;2006 were not included in the computation of diluted income per
share because they were anti-dilutive.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Options to purchase
1,822,000 shares of common stock with an exercise price in excess of $4.62 per
share outstanding during fiscal&nbsp;2005 were not included in the computation
of diluted income per share because they were anti-dilutive.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The unrealized losses on available-for-sale securities
as of April&nbsp;30, 2006 are recorded in accumulated other comprehensive
income (loss) of the consolidated statements of stockholders&#146; equity and
comprehensive income, net of tax.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
financial instruments in short-term investments are highly liquid and can be
converted to cash and cash equivalents without restriction and, accordingly,
are classified as current assets in the accompanying consolidated balance
sheets.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 6&#151;Leases<a name="Note6leases_123405"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At April&nbsp;29, 2007, the Company had a federal net
operating loss carryforward of approximately $1.0 million available to offset
future taxable income that expires between fiscal 2018 and 2025 if not
utilized.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At April&nbsp;29, 2007, the Company had approximately
$2.6&nbsp;million and $1.9&nbsp;million of federal and state research and
development credit carryovers, respectively, available to offset future taxable
income. The federal credits expire between fiscal&nbsp;2009 and 2027 if not
utilized. The state credits carryovers are indefinite. At April&nbsp;29, 2007,
the Company has a federal alternative minimum tax credit of $177,000, which can
be carried forward indefinitely.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the Internal Revenue Code Section&nbsp;382, the
amounts of and benefits from net operating loss and tax credit carryforwards
may be impaired or limited in certain circumstances. Events which cause limitations
in the amount of net operating losses and tax credit carryforwards that the
Company may utilize in any one year include, but are not limited to, a
cumulative ownership change of more than 50%, as defined, over a three-year
period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During fiscal 2006, the
Company reversed approximately $226,000 of tax reserves upon expiry of the
statute of limitations. These tax reserves had been established to allow for
potential tax exposures relating to the level of income apportioned to
California in the Company&#146;s state tax returns.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 8&#151;Stockholders&#146;
Equity<a name="Note8stockholdersEquity_125142"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Common and Preferred Stock</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company was originally
incorporated in California in October&nbsp;1985 and reincorporated in Delaware
in May&nbsp;1993. The Board of Directors approved a recapitalization that
authorized 45&nbsp;million shares of common stock and 2&nbsp;million shares of
undesignated preferred stock. In December&nbsp;1996, the Board of Directors
designated 60,000 shares of preferred stock as Series&nbsp;A Participating
Preferred Stock. The Board of Directors has the authority to determine the
powers, preferences, rights and the qualifications, limitations or restrictions
granted to or imposed upon any wholly unissued shares of undesignated preferred
stock, without any further vote or action by the Company&#146;s shareholders.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CATALYST SEMICONDUCTOR, INC.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Secondary Public Offering</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company completed a
secondary public offering of its common stock in July&nbsp;2004. The Company
sold 1,450,000 common shares at $6.00 per share. Proceeds to the Company, net
of underwriting discounts and commissions and related offering expenses of
$714,000 were approximately $8.0 million. In connection with this transaction,
Elex N.V., a related party and other selling stockholders sold 2,850,000 and
300,000 common shares, respectively, at $6.00 per share. In aggregate,
4,600,000 common shares were sold</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stockholder Rights Plan</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2006, our
board of directors adopted a stockholder rights plan with a term of ten years
which will expire in December&nbsp;2016. Under this plan, we issued a dividend
of one right for each share of our common stock. Each right initially entitles
stockholders to purchase one one-thousandth of a share of our preferred stock
for $18.00. However, the rights are not immediately exercisable. If a person or
group acquires, or announces a tender or exchange offer that would result in
the acquisition of 15% of our common stock, unless the rights are redeemed by
us for $0.01 per right, the rights will become exercisable by all rights
holders, except the acquiring person or group, for shares of our common stock
or the stock of the third party acquirer having a value of twice the right&#146;s
then-current exercise price.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Common Stock Option Exchange Offer</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;16, 2007, the Company repriced employee
stock option awards. Under the terms of this repricing, the Company repriced
certain employee stock options having an exercise price of greater than $4.00
to an exercise price of $3.35, the trading stock price fair value on the date
of the exchange. All options tendered received a non-statutory stock option to
purchase one (1)&nbsp;share for every two (2)&nbsp;exchanged incentive or
non-statutory stock options pursuant to the exchange offer. In consideration
for the repricing of these eligible stock option awards, employees were
required to return their previously awarded options for cancellation. Regardless
of whether the original options were vested, the new options vest as to 1/36th
of the shares subject to the new option each month commencing one month after
the new option grant date of March&nbsp;16, 2007, and have a contractual term
of 10 years beginning on that date.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has accounted
for the repricing and cancellation transactions as a modification under SFAS No.&nbsp;123(R).
In accordance with SFAS No.&nbsp;123(R), the Company will record the
incremental fair value related to the repriced awards, together with
unamortized stock-based compensation expense associated with the unvested
cancelled awards, over the remaining requisite service period of the option
holders. Seventy eight employees participated in this program. A total of
1,545,538 shares were cancelled for 772,769 newly issued non-statutory stock
options. The incremental fair value of the repricing was approximately
$117,000, which will be recognized on a straight-line basis over the new
requisite service period of 36 months.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 9&#151;Employee
Benefit Plan<a name="Note9employeeBenefitPlan_125328"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2004, the
Company implemented a Section&nbsp;401(k)&nbsp;Plan. The 401(k)&nbsp;Plan
provides participating employees with an opportunity to accumulate funds for
retirement and hardship. The 401(k)&nbsp;Plan provides for a 25% matching
contribution which vests immediately. In fiscal&nbsp;2007, fiscal 2006 and
fiscal&nbsp;2005, the Company made matching contributions of $208,000, $190,000
and $192,000, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Distributors and resellers
have accounted for a significant portion of the Company&#146;s net revenues in the
past. For fiscal 2007, sales to Avnet Inc., an international distributor,
represented 10.3% of the Company&#146;s net revenues. For fiscal 2006, sales to
Avnet represented 11.8% of the Company&#146;s net revenues. For fiscal 2005, none of
the Company&#146;s customers represented 10% or more of the Company&#146;s net revenues.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CATALYST SEMICONDUCTOR, INC.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 11&#151;Commitments
and Contingencies<a name="Note11commitmentsAndContingencies_125732"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchase Commitments</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchase commitments for
open purchase orders at April&nbsp;29, 2007 and April&nbsp;30, 2006 for which
goods and services had not been received were approximately $5.9 million and
$6.2 million, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Litigation and Other Claims</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the normal course of
business, the Company periodically receives notification of threats of legal
action in relation to claims of patent infringement by the Company. Currently
there are no such active actions.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Guarantees</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In November&nbsp;2002, the
FASB issued FASB Interpretation No.&nbsp;45,<i>
&#147;Guarantor&#146;s Accounting and Disclosure Requirements for Guarantees, Including
Indirect Guarantees of Indebtedness of Others&#148;</i> (&#147;FIN&nbsp;45&#148;). The
Company applies the disclosure provisions of FIN 45 to its agreements that
contain guarantee or indemnification clauses. FIN&nbsp;45 requires that a
liability be recorded in the guarantor&#146;s balance sheet upon issuance of a
guarantee. In addition, FIN&nbsp;45 requires disclosures about the guarantees
that an entity has issued, including a reconciliation of changes in the entity&#146;s
product warranty liabilities. These disclosure provisions expand those required
by SFAS No.&nbsp;5,<i> &#147;Accounting for
Contingencies&#148;</i> by requiring that guarantors disclose certain types
of guarantees, even if the likelihood of requiring the guarantor&#146;s performance
is remote. The following is a description of significant arrangements through
which the Company is a guarantor:</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 50.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Indemnification
Obligations</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is a party to a variety of agreements
pursuant to which it may be obligated to indemnify the other party with respect
to certain matters. Typically, these obligations arise in the context of
contracts entered into by the Company, under which the Company customarily
agrees to hold the other party harmless against losses arising from a breach of
representations and covenants related to such matters as title to assets sold
and certain intellectual property rights. Generally, payment by the Company is
conditioned on the other party making a claim pursuant to the procedures
specified in the particular contract, which procedures typically allow the
Company to challenge the other party&#146;s claims. Further, the Company&#146;s
obligations under these agreements may be limited in terms of time and/or
amount, and in some instances, the Company may have recourse against third
parties for certain payments made by it under these agreements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">It is not possible to
predict the maximum potential amount of future payments under these or similar
agreements due to the conditional nature of the Company&#146;s obligations and the
unique facts and circumstances involved in each particular agreement. Historically,
payments made by the Company under these agreements have not had a material
effect on its business, financial condition, cash flows or results of
operations. The Company believes that if it were to incur a loss in any of
these matters, such loss should not have a material effect on its business,
financial condition, cash flows or results of operations.</font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-26</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-26',FILE='C:\Fc\19411354355_P66506CHE_2250209\18586-1-fq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Jul 13 11:37 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">CATALYST SEMICONDUCTOR, INC.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 50.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Product Warranties</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company estimates its
product warranty costs based on historical warranty claim experience and
applies this estimate to the revenue stream for products under warranty. Included
in the Company&#146;s sales returns reserves are estimated return exposures
associated with product warranties. Estimated future costs for warranties
applicable to revenues recognized in the current period are charged to the
Company&#146;s cost of revenues. The warranty accrual is reviewed quarterly to
verify that it properly reflects the remaining obligations based on the
anticipated expenditures over the balance of the obligation period. Adjustments
are made when actual claim experience differs from estimates. Warranty costs
were less than $100,000 for each of fiscal 2007, fiscal 2006 and fiscal 2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 12&#151;Related
Party Transactions<a name="Note12relatedPartyTransactions_130113"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Elex N.V.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2000, the Company
began taking delivery of wafers fabricated at X-FAB Texas,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;X-FAB&#148;)
a wholly owned subsidiary of Elex N.V. (&#147;Elex&#148;), a Belgian holding company. Roland
Duch&#226;telet, the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Elex, serves as a
member of the Company&#146;s Board of Directors. Elex initially became a related
party in 1998 through the purchase of 5.5&nbsp;million restricted shares of the
Company&#146;s common stock. The wafers provided by X-FAB include most of the
Company&#146;s analog/mixed-signal products and supplement some of the same
EEPROM designs fabricated at various other foundries the Company utilizes. Other
than purchase orders currently open with X-FAB, there is no purchasing
agreement in place with X-FAB. During fiscal&nbsp;2007, fiscal&nbsp;2006
and fiscal&nbsp;2005, the Company purchased $1.2 million, $2.5 million and
$2.4&nbsp;million of wafers, respectively, from X-FAB. As of April&nbsp;29,
2007 and April&nbsp;30, 2006, the total amount owed to X-FAB by the
Company was approximately $68,000 and $143,000, respectively. Elex held 4.5% of
the outstanding shares of the Company as of April&nbsp;29, 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company believes that the terms of these
transactions were no less favorable than reasonably could be expected to be
obtained from unaffiliated parties.</font></p>
